precepts.text: Later in history king Ahaziah walked in the ways of the house of Ahab, for his mother was his counsellor to do wickedly; the same pattern seen with Micah's mother.
precepts.point: A mother buying her son idols was nothing new in Israel; there were mothers who steered a son down the wrong path.

note.label: Judges 17: Micah's House of Idols and the Hired Levite

precepts.why:
Micah’s mother, instead of rebuking a son who stole eleven hundred shekels of silver from her, said “Blessed be thou of the Lord, my son”, and had a graven image and a molten image made to set up in his house. A mother buying her son idols was nothing new in Israel. Later in history king Ahaziah “walked in the ways of the house of Ahab: for his mother was his counsellor to do wickedly.”

It is the same pattern. There were mothers in Israel who steered a son down the wrong path, and Micah’s mother was one of them, counselling her son into idolatry with the very silver he had stolen from her.

points: A man of mount Ephraim named Micah stole eleven hundred shekels of silver from his own mother, and when he heard her cursing about the missing silver he confessed, I took it, and restored it to her.
A mother buying her son idols was nothing new in Israel; there were mothers who steered a son down the wrong path.

note.label: Judges 17: Micah's House of Idols and the Hired Levite

points: Instead of rebuking her son, his mother said blessed be thou of the LORD, and told him she had wholly dedicated the silver for him to make a graven image and a molten image. She refused to keep what he returned, took two hundred shekels to the founder, and had idols made to set up in her son's house.

note.label: Judges 17: Micah's House of Idols and the Hired Levite

points: Micah had a whole house of gods. He made an ephod and teraphim and consecrated one of his own sons to be his priest, a counterfeit priesthood serving counterfeit gods.

note.label: Judges 17: Micah's House of Idols and the Hired Levite

points: This verse is the key to understanding the whole book of Judges. With no king and no government, Israel was sheep without a shepherd, and when you see how the people carry on in these chapters, that is why: every man did that which was right in his own eyes.

The same individual spirit is around today in those who say join no camp and let no man teach you. Every time the scripture shows Israel without a leadership structure, all manner of wickedness follows, primarily idolatry.

note.label: Judges 17: Micah's House of Idols and the Hired Levite

points: A young Levite of Bethlehemjudah departed to sojourn wherever he could find a place and came to mount Ephraim to the house of Micah.

note.label: Judges 17: Micah's House of Idols and the Hired Levite

points: When Micah learned the man was a Levite, of the tribe known for the priesthood and the knowledge of the sacrifices, he offered him a deal: dwell with me, be unto me a father and a priest, ten shekels of silver by the year, a suit of apparel, and thy victuals. He hired himself a personal priest for his idols.

note.label: Judges 17: Micah's House of Idols and the Hired Levite

points: The Levite was content to dwell with him and became as one of his sons. Nothing says the Levite was already in idolatry, but when money was offered he went right along with it; being corrupted for reward was always the Levites' weakness.

note.label: Judges 17: Micah's House of Idols and the Hired Levite

points: Then Micah said, now know I that the LORD will do me good, seeing I have a Levite to my priest. A house full of idols and a hired priest over them, yet he expected the Most High to bless him because a Levite was on the payroll. That is how sick in the mind Israel was without leadership.
